newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money nudges up, conditions tighten.
newsitem.headline: German call money nudges up, conditions tighten.

text.p: Tighter liquidity conditions helped move German overnight rates slightly higher on Tuesday to trade between 3.05/3.075, but dealers did not expect lasting implications from the higher rates.
Rates were trading slightly higher from Monday's three percent rate, dealers said, explaining that the upcoming tax payment date was putting extra pressure on the system.

But dealers also said that funds should be flowing back into the system during the course of the day which should help alleviate any extreme tightness. Dealers were unable to predict how much money the Bundesbank may inject into the system.
A repo pact for 65 billion marks set at a fixed three percent expires on Wednesday.
But dealers said uncertainty about reserve holdings prevented them from formulating a clear picture about how much money the central bank bank may inject into the system.

The Bundesbank said reserves on Friday stood at 38.0 billion marks compared with 37.8 billion on Thursday. The monthly average stood at 38.6 billion marks on Sunday compared with 39.0 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set unchanged at 3.09667 percent on Tuesday. --Frankfurt Newsroom
